findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`, so the guard never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only calls `include_<attr>?` hooks. The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is dead code. `website_name` is serialized even when the website is blank. It also bypasses the TL0 `untrusted_attributes` restriction, because `website_name` is not in that list. Anonymous viewers therefore see the website host of a restricted TL0 user, even though `website` itself is hidden. Fix: rename the method to `include_website_name?` and add the untrusted check, or add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: `<<` mutates a string and the suffix check is fragile
findings.body: `"." << website_host` creates a new literal and appends to it, which works but is confusing and breaks under frozen string literals. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. The branch's intent is also unclear: it only checks that the website host is a parent domain suffix of the instance host. The sibling-subdomain branch compares only host label counts, so `a.example.com` and `b.other.example.com` style cases are handled inconsistently. For example, `www.example.co.uk` versus `forum.example.co.uk` behaves differently from the equal-length case.

findings.title: Path appended without normalization
findings.body: A website of `http://example.com/` yields `example.com/` with a trailing slash, and a URL with a query string or fragment drops them. Only the path is appended, so the display name is inconsistent. A URL with no path gives `example.com` plus an empty string, which is fine, but the trailing-slash case is shown awkwardly.
